main_result.nested_family_envelope_theorem: For each reporting channel j, V3 e-CIs are nested in alpha. If every candidate selected alpha satisfies alpha_{j,k}<=beta_j for fixed precommitted caps beta_1+beta_2<=delta, then for any same-history data-dependent selector k_hat, selected-channel miscoverage is a subset of the cap-level miscoverage event. Therefore P(any selected bound misses)<=beta_1+beta_2<=delta, with no independence assumption and no factor K.
main_result.near_tightness: With two independent valid e-values taking 1/.025 with probability .025 and 0 otherwise, an adversarial selector that favors whichever extreme channel is high has any-selected-miscoverage probability 1-.975^2=.049375. Thus the symmetric .025/.025 coordinate envelope is nearly tight under arbitrary selection without further structural assumptions.
main_result.dominance_caveat: The common-scaled nine-grid is valid but, for pure interval width/stopping utility, every one of its pairs has channel alphas <=.025 and is therefore weakly dominated by the single fixed balanced pair (.025,.025). More generally, under precommitted caps beta_1,beta_2 with beta_1+beta_2=.05, the cap pair itself dominates every candidate lying coordinatewise below it. So the envelope correction removes the K penalty but also removes the statistical reason to post-select among under-cap splits.
main_result.interpretation: The earlier uniform pi=1/9 construction remains valid but is much more conservative than necessary because it counts nested intervals within a channel as distinct error opportunities. However, a simple K-free envelope does not deliver useful adaptive allocation: its dominant point is just the precommitted cap split. Meaningful same-history adaptive allocation still needs a selection-rule-specific proof, or pilot-freeze-fresh-confirm.

preliminary_local_v3_cost.execution_status: Eight-campaign direct-array transcription of frozen V3 mathematics; repository-exact checked-out validation still pending.
preliminary_local_v3_cost.interpretation: In this small family the envelope-scaled grid resolved on exactly the same eight paths/times as fixed .025/.025, illustrating the dominance point. Fresh confirmation retained genuine allocation adaptivity but paid a reset cost; pairwise 1/9 insurance was far slower.

measurement_validity_rules: Exploit nesting before applying a generic multiple-comparisons union bound; duplicated alpha levels for the same parameter family are not independent error opportunities.

A K-free coordinate-envelope guarantee is valid for arbitrary same-history selection, but if all candidate intervals are monotone in alpha then the cap pair dominates every under-cap candidate; do not mistake validity flexibility for statistical power.
Meaningful adaptive alpha allocation that can outperform a well-chosen fixed cap split requires extra selection structure, fresh confirmation, or a different reporting target.
scope_guards: The near-tightness construction concerns arbitrary selectors, not the deployed fastest-safe selector specifically.
The dominance claim is for reporting objectives monotone in each channel alpha, such as narrower one-sided bounds or earlier threshold crossing, with the same underlying V3 evidence.
The eight-campaign numeric comparison is preliminary and synthetic.
